Arian Kabashi is a Swedish professional footballer of Kosovar-Albanian descent, born on **March 26, 1996**, in **Helsingborg, Sweden**. He is primarily a **winger** or **attacking midfielder**, known for his pace, dribbling, and technical ability. Here’s a detailed overview of his career and background:

---

### **Early Life & Background**
- **Full Name**: Arian Kabashi
- **Date of Birth**: March 26, 1996
- **Place of Birth**: Helsingborg, Sweden
- **Nationality**: Swedish (eligible for Kosovo and Albania)
- **Ethnicity**: Kosovar-Albanian (his parents are from Kosovo)
- **Youth Career**: Started at **Helsingborgs IF**, one of Sweden’s most prominent youth academies.

---

### **Senior Career**
#### **1. Helsingborgs IF (2014–2017)**
- **Debut**: Made his **Allsvenskan (Swedish top division)** debut in **2014** at age 18.
- **Breakthrough**: Became a regular in the 2015 season, scoring **3 goals in 22 appearances**.
- **2016 Season**: Played a key role in Helsingborg’s **Superettan (second division)** campaign after relegation, helping them secure promotion back to Allsvenskan.
- **Total Apps/Goals**: **60+ appearances, 5+ goals** for Helsingborg.

#### **2. Östersunds FK (2017–2019)**
- **Transfer**: Joined **Östersunds FK** in **2017**, a club known for its rapid rise in Swedish football under manager **Graham Potter**.
- **Performance**: Struggled for consistent game time but contributed in **Europa League** qualifiers (Östersund reached the **Round of 32 in 2017–18**).
- **Loan to Dalkurd FF (2018)**: Spent the second half of the 2018 season on loan at **Dalkurd FF** (then in Allsvenskan), making **10 appearances**.
- **Total Apps/Goals**: **30+ appearances, 2 goals** for Östersund.

#### **3. Return to Helsingborgs IF (2019–2020)**
- **Re-signing**: Returned to Helsingborg in **2019** after their relegation to Superettan.
- **Role**: Featured sporadically, making **15 appearances** without scoring.
- **Departure**: Left in **2020** after Helsingborg’s promotion back to Allsvenskan.

#### **4. Varbergs BoIS (2020–2021)**
- **Move**: Joined **Varbergs BoIS** (newly promoted to Allsvenskan) in **2020**.
- **Performance**: Played **18 matches** in the 2020 season but struggled for impact.
- **2021 Season**: Featured in **10 games** before leaving mid-season.

#### **5. GAIS (2021–2022)**
- **Loan**: Joined **GAIS** (Superettan) on loan in **2021**, making **12 appearances**.
- **Permanent Move**: Signed permanently in **2022** but played only **5 games** before leaving.

#### **6. Landskrona BoIS (2022–2023)**
- **Transfer**: Moved to **Landskrona BoIS** (Superettan) in **2022**.
- **Performance**: Became a key player, scoring **4 goals in 25 appearances** in the 2022 season.
- **2023 Season**: Played **10 games** before departing.

#### **7. IFK Värnamo (2023–Present)**
- **Current Club**: Joined **IFK Värnamo** (Allsvenskan) in **July 2023** on a **short-term contract** (until December 2023).
- **Role**: Mostly used as a **substitute**, making **10+ appearances** in the 2023 season.
- **Contract Extension**: Signed a **new 1-year deal** in **December 2023**, keeping him until **2024**.

---

### **International Career**
- **Youth Level**: Represented **Sweden at U17 and U19 levels**.
- **Senior Level**:
  - **Eligible for Kosovo and Albania** (through his Kosovar-Albanian heritage) but has **not** been capped at senior level for any national team.
  - In **2016**, he was called up to the **Kosovo national team** for a friendly but did not debut.
  - Has not been called up since, likely due to his **lack of consistent club form**.

---

### **Playing Style**
- **Position**: Primarily a **left winger** but can also play as a **right winger** or **attacking midfielder**.
- **Strengths**:
  - **Dribbling & Pace**: Quick and agile, good at taking on defenders.
  - **Technique**: Strong ball control and passing in tight spaces.
  - **Creativity**: Capable of providing assists and unlocking defenses.
- **Weaknesses**:
  - **Inconsistency**: Struggled to maintain form at higher levels.
  - **Defensive Work Rate**: Not known for tracking back.
  - **Injury Prone**: Has had periods of limited game time due to minor injuries.

---

### **Career Statistics (Approximate)**
| **Club**            | **League**       | **Apps** | **Goals** |
|---------------------|------------------|----------|-----------|
| Helsingborgs IF     | Allsvenskan/Superettan | 60+      | 5+        |
| Östersunds FK       | Allsvenskan      | 30+      | 2         |
| Dalkurd FF (loan)   | Allsvenskan      | 10       | 0         |
| Varbergs BoIS       | Allsvenskan      | 28       | 0         |
| GAIS                | Superettan       | 17       | 0         |
| Landskrona BoIS     | Superettan       | 35       | 4         |
| IFK Värnamo         | Allsvenskan      | 10+      | 0         |

*(Note: Exact stats may vary slightly depending on sources.)*

---

### **Personal Life & Trivia**
- **Family**: His younger brother, **Arbnor Kabashi**, is also a footballer (plays for **Helsingborgs IF** in Superettan).
- **Social Media**: Active on **Instagram (@arian_kabashi)** but not highly followed.
- **Nickname**: Sometimes called **"Ari"** by fans.
- **Injuries**: Has had minor injury setbacks throughout his career, affecting his consistency.

---

### **Current Status (2024)**
- **Club**: IFK Värnamo (Allsvenskan)
- **Contract**: Until **December 2024**
- **Role**: Mostly a **bench player** but provides depth in attack.
- **Future**: At **28 years old**, he is in the latter stages of his career. If he doesn’t secure a starting role, he may move to a lower-division club or abroad (possibly in the Balkans or lower-tier European leagues).

---

### **Summary**
Arian Kabashi is a **talented but inconsistent** winger who has played for several Swedish clubs, mostly in **Allsvenskan and Superettan**. While he showed promise early in his career, he has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter at the top level. His **Kosovar-Albanian heritage** makes him eligible for national team call-ups, but he has yet to make an international breakthrough.
